summary.text: Jeremy Moss is the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 11th District and a Michigan state senator from Southfield. A former Southfield city councilmember and state representative, he has served in the Legislature since 2015, including as Senate President Pro Tem. He is running on healthcare costs, the cost of living and opposition to Trump administration immigration enforcement.

paragraphs.text: Moss is a lifelong Oakland County resident and a graduate of Groves High School, according to his campaign website, and he lives in Southfield.

He earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Michigan State University, where his campaign website says he took part in student humanitarian missions, and then worked under then-Southfield Mayor Brenda Lawrence.
Elected to the Southfield City Council in 2011, he was, his campaign website says, its youngest-ever member.
Moss won election to the Michigan House of Representatives (District 35) in 2014 and served from 2015 to 2019.
He then won the Michigan Senate seat for District 11 in 2018 and was elected in 2022 to represent District 7, a term that ends in January 2027; he is not seeking re-election to that seat.
In the Senate he chairs the Elections Committee and the Senate Regulatory Reform Committee (2025-2026), and earlier terms included chairing the Elections and Ethics Committee.

His campaign website says he led the 2022 effort to win a Democratic Michigan Senate majority, served as Senate President Pro Tem, and sponsored the most bills signed into law among state legislators in 2023.
Moss won the Democratic primary for Michigan's open 11th District on August 4, 2026, and faces Republican Ethan Baker in November.
